translations.text: The Book of Susanna.
There was a man living in Babylon whose name was Joakim.
He married a woman named Susanna, the daughter of Helena. She was very beautiful and feared the Lord.
All her family were righteous, and they taught their daughter all the commandments of Moses.
Her husband Joakim was extremely wealthy. He had a garden around his house, and the Jews used to gather at his home, because he was more distinguished than any of them at that time.

Two elders arose among the people who were wealthy members of the community and judges that year. It was about them that God said, “Wickedness came out of Babylon, from the elders and judges who served in the temple.”
These men regularly came to Joakim’s house. Everyone who had a legal dispute also came there to have the case heard.
When all the people had left at midday, Susanna would go with her maids into her husband’s garden.
Those elders saw her every day as she walked and went into her husband’s garden.
They lusted after her, and their minds became perverted. They lowered their eyes so that they would not look toward heaven or be remembered again among the righteous.
Both of them lusted after her, wanting to be with her as a man is with a woman, but they did not reveal their affliction to one another,
because they wanted to be with her secretly.
Every day they eagerly watched for her, hoping to see her.
One said to his companion, “Let us leave here, because it is time for the meal.”

They went out to leave together, but each slipped away from the other. Both turned back without knowing what the other was doing, and they met each other there. Ashamed of the deception they had practiced on each other, they sat down and disclosed to one another their unrestrained and destructive desire: how they lusted after this woman who was full of modesty. From then on, they waited for an opportunity to find her alone and dishonor this woman who deserved to be remembered well.

While they were watching for her, they saw her going out as she did every day, just as she had yesterday and the day before, with her two maids accompanying her. She wanted to bathe there in the gardens because it was hot. Those elders went and hid in ambush there in the garden.
There was no one else in the garden except those two elders.
Susanna said to her maids, “Go and bring me oil and soap, and close the garden gates while I bathe.”
They did as she had instructed them, closed the garden gate, and went to fetch what they had been told to bring. They did not see the elders who were hiding there.
When Susanna's maids had gone out, those elders rushed at her and said to her,
“Look, the garden gates are closed, and there is no one to see us. We desire you intensely, so sleep with us.
But if you are unwilling to sleep with us, we will testify falsely against you that a young man slept with you, and that this was why you sent your maids away.”

Susanna thought it over and said, “I am trapped on every side. If I do this, it means death for me before God, because I will have dishonored the bed of my husband Joakim. But if I do not do it, I will suffer a terrible death at your hands, along with a bad reputation unworthy of my freeborn status. I will leave my whole family in shame because of the false testimony of wicked men, who add to Israel’s ruin and misery by making it a mockery among foreign nations.
But it is better for me to die unjustly at your hands than to sin before the Lord, from whom nothing is hidden. I trust in him to rescue me even from your hands.”
Susanna cried out loudly because of the distress those depraved men were causing her, and the elders also shouted against her.
One of them ran and opened the gates of the garden.

When this shouting was heard in the garden, the members of Susanna’s household quickly ran inside to see what had happened to her. When all Susanna’s people had gathered, the elders began to testify falsely against her: “As we were passing outside the garden, we looked in to see the garden, and we saw Susanna with a young man lying with her. We ran to seize them, but we could not seize the young man because he was stronger than we were.”
When all Susanna’s people heard the elders’ words, they were ashamed of what the elders said she had done.

The next day, all the people gathered at the home of her husband Joakim to investigate Susanna’s case. If she really had committed this indecent act and dishonored the bed of her husband Joakim, she was to die. Both those elders also came to accuse her unjustly.
They said before all the people, “Send for Susanna, the daughter of Helkanah, Joakim’s wife.” So they sent for her.
She came with her whole family, all her acquaintances, and her friends, and stood in the middle of the entire assembly of the people.
The woman was very beautiful in appearance and humbler than all other women. Her clothing was very modest.
When those wicked men saw her, they ordered her veil to be removed so that they could satisfy themselves with her beauty, even if only by looking.
Everyone who saw her was weeping, together with all her people.
While a large crowd surrounded her, the two elders came in and gave false testimony against her. They laid their hands on Susanna’s head and said, “We saw this woman sleeping with a young man.”
Susanna, deeply distressed by what had happened to her, lifted her eyes toward heaven, to the Lord, because her heart was set on God.

The two elders said, “Yesterday, while we were walking outside the garden, Susanna came with her two servant girls, and they entered the garden. She sent her servant girls away and shut the garden gates.
Then a young man who had been hiding came to her and lay with her.
We had entered the garden, and we saw the deceit and ran toward them.
“We found them lying together, but we could not seize the young man because he was stronger than we were. He opened the garden gate and ran away.
“But we seized this woman and asked her, ‘Who was that young man who was sleeping with you?’ She refused to tell us who he was. These are the things we testify against her before you.”

The whole assembly believed them as elders of the people and as judges. They condemned Susanna to death so that all women would be afraid and would no longer bring such disgrace upon themselves and their families.
Susanna cried out in a loud voice and said, “God, who knows all things, before whom hidden things lie open, who knows what is to come before it happens—

“may he see that these men have falsely accused me. Here I am, about to die, although I have done none of the things they have testified against me. This is only because I did not do what they wanted, what they asked of me.”
The Lord heard Susanna’s cry.
As she was going out to die, God immediately sent his Holy Spirit upon a young boy named Daniel.
He cried out in a loud voice and said, “I am innocent of this woman’s blood, because she is innocent of this filthy act.”
The whole assembly turned toward him and said to him, “What is this that you have said?”
Standing among them, he spoke and said, “Are you so foolish, people of Israel, that you do not judge the daughters of Israel justly?”
Return to the court, for you have falsely condemned this woman.
The whole assembly returned to the court. Those elders said to Daniel, “Come, sit among us and tell us. Let us see, for God has given you the standing of an elder.”

Daniel said to the whole assembly, “Separate these elders from one another for me. Then I will judge them as God has enabled me, and I will show that they have wickedly given false testimony against Susanna.”
The assembly separated them from one another. He called one of them and said to him, “You are a man who has grown old in wicked days. Now the sins you committed long ago have caught up with you:
“you passed unjust judgments, condemned the righteous, destroyed the humble, acquitted the guilty, and condemned the innocent.
“Now tell me this before this whole assembly: under which tree did you see this woman and that young man lying together?” The elder said to him, “Under a pistachio tree.”
Daniel said to him, “Know this: if you have indeed lied, it will come down upon your own head. For the angel of God is [?], having received a command from God to split you from end to end.”
Afterward he called the other man, his companion, and said to him also, “Offspring of Canaan and not of Judah! This woman’s beauty enslaved you, and desire for her turned your heart astray.
“This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and out of fear they would carry out your wicked desires.

“But you, tell me before this whole assembly: under which tree did you see this woman and that young man lying together?” He answered before the whole assembly, “Under a pomegranate tree.” The whole assembly cried out together in a loud voice and praised the Lord, who reveals hidden things, rewards the innocent according to their innocence, repays wrongdoers, and brings a person’s conduct down upon his own head.

Daniel said to him, “You have indeed spoken wickedly before the Lord against this defenseless woman. You wanted to shed innocent blood unjustly. But now your wickedness will come down upon your own head, as it is written in the law of Moses. For look, the angel of God has been sent against you, holding a sword in his hand, to split you from end to end and destroy both of you together.”
The whole assembly answered together in a loud voice, “Glory to God, who has saved all who have believed in his name!”
Daniel exposed the wrong they had done, and the whole assembly rose against them.
They dealt with the men according to Moses’ command and put them to death. The Lord brought evil retribution upon them, as they deserved, and innocent blood was saved that day.

Elkanah and his wife rejoiced over their daughter Susanna, Joakim’s wife, because no wrongdoing was found in her. All the people and Susanna’s entire family praised God because the disgrace of wrongdoing had been removed from them.

Daniel grew in stature and favor before Susanna’s entire family and in the eyes of the whole congregation of Israel. He always practiced justice and righteousness. The fame of his praiseworthy deeds was spoken of among all the people, along with the hidden and secret things that he had discerned.
The book of Susanna is finished.
